title: [4/11/2025] Frequency of Internet usage in a particular country
prompt: The table shows the frequency of adults using the internet in one European country from 2006 to 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the frequency with which adults accessed the internet in a European country over a five-year period from 2006 to 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was a clear upward trend in daily and weekly internet usage throughout the period, while the percentage of people who occasionally (three times a month) and never used the internet declined dramatically. By 2010, the majority of adults were daily internet users, compared to a minority of non-users.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the more frequent internet users, in 2006, 36% of adults used the internet on a daily basis, which was more than twice the figure for weekly users, at 15%. The daily usage figure then rose consistently year on year, reaching 45% in 2008 before surging to 72% in 2010, representing a doubling of the initial figure. In contrast, the proportion of weekly users, while initially increasing to 29% in 2008, subsequently fell back to 22% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the less frequent internet users, both categories showed declining trends. In 2006, 34% of adults never used the internet, which was more than double the figure for those who used it three times a month, at 15%. The percentage of people who never went online then fell sharply to 20% in 2007 and continued to decrease dramatically to just 1% by 2010. Meanwhile, the three-times-monthly users declined more gradually, from 15% in 2006 to 5% in 2010, with the most significant drop occurring between 2007 and 2008, when the figure fell by 5 percentage points.
